raw_response:
Ai, you want me to tell you how I do my land this year? Alright, sit down. I been on this dirt 50 years, so I don't think too hard about it no more. I do what works.

Me and the old lady, just the two of us now. Kids moved to the city long ago. Twenty mu of ground. My back and knees ain't what they used to be, but we manage.

I split it like this: about 15 mu I do wheat and maize together, one after the other, like everyone in the village. The other 5 mu I still got in cotton, though I tell you, the picking is getting too hard. Maybe next year I give it up, put it all in wheat-maize. We'll see.

**The wheat** — I plant middle of October, same time as everybody. Before I plant, I spread one bag of the compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 stuff from the supply shop in town. Then in the spring, when it starts coming up tall at jointing, I put out some urea on top, maybe half a bag per mu. Water it three times — once before the freeze if the ground is dry, once at jointing, once when the grain is filling up. Harvest beginning of June. If it's a good year, I get maybe 400 kg the mu. Bad year, less. Last year was okay.

**The maize** — soon as wheat comes off, we gotta move fast. Only three, four days to get it in the ground, or you miss the window. No time to plow deep, I just have the tractor fella do a quick pass and broadcast the seed with some compound fertilizer, one bag the mu. Later on in July I throw down a little urea if the leaves look yellow. Water maybe once if the summer rains don't come. Comes off end of September. Gets about 400 kg the mu, usually.

**The cotton** — that's the hard one. Plant end of April when the soil's warm. Put down fertilizer before, less than wheat, cotton don't eat as much. Spray for the bollworm four, five times through summer — if you don't spray, you lose it all, I seen it happen. Picking starts September, goes into October, three or four rounds. My niece sometimes comes back weekends to help. Gets maybe 230 kg the mu of seed cotton in a decent year.

**Seed** — I buy fresh from the shop. I can't read the packages, so I just tell the shopkeeper "same as last year" and he knows me. He gives me the wheat the village plants. Maize has to be the hybrid, one year only, I know that much.

**Money** — it's tight. Pension and what the land gives, that's it. Can't afford to waste fertilizer, but I also won't skimp too much — I learned young, that year we had the light grain because I tried to save, lost more than I saved. So I put about what I always put, no more, no less.
